character.name: Bettina Hobbleton
character.role: Head Waiter of the Full House
character.description: A tall, folded person in a uniform that belongs to a different job, carrying a bag that clinks in an administrative way. Bettina is a Head Waiter of the Full House and every table has been booked since the place opened, by people who have never come.

npc.narrative: You reach the stile beneath le stelle, where una lanterna burns beside molte sedie, all empty. Bettina Hobbleton counts you on one dito and seems faintly let down by the uno. The nearest paese is nine panini away, she adds, which is nothing at night.
npc.native: Buonasera, qui tutti vogliono prenotare un tavolo, ma nessuno viene mai. Come antipasto c'è il pane, come primo c'è la zuppa, ma spesso è fredda o troppo salata. Che cosa vuole fare stasera, e che cosa mangia per cominciare? Come va la sua serata, e che cosa mi dice se la zuppa è così?
npc.translation: Good evening, here everybody wants to book a table, but nobody ever comes. As a starter there is bread, as a first course there is soup, but often it is cold or too salty. What do you want to do tonight, and what do you eat to begin with? How is your evening going, and what do you tell me if the soup is like that?

player: Buonasera! La mia serata va bene, grazie. Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per una persona, per favore.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Bettina, said your evening is going well, and asked to book a table in clear Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you said you would like to book a table with "Vorrei prenotare un tavolo".

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per una persona, per favore.

objectiveResults.feedback: You didn't say what you will have to start with yet; Bettina will ask again later.
You didn't say what is wrong with the soup, whether it is cold or too salty; Bettina will ask again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Bettina what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Bettina asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Bettina that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: You stop at the tavolo by the finestra, where a small brass card says prenotato in a hand older than the sedia. Bettina counts the stelle through the glass and seems pleased the total is odd. The cucina is two sandwiches away, and the candela is doing its best.
npc.native: Benissimo, un tavolo per una persona, e lei viene davvero! Come antipasto abbiamo il pane e il prosciutto, e come primo c'è la zuppa, ma la zuppa è spesso fredda o troppo salata. Che cosa prende per cominciare, e che cosa dice se la zuppa arriva così? Che cosa pensa di questo posto?
npc.translation: Very good, a table for one person, and you really are coming! As a starter we have bread and ham, and as a first course there is the soup, but the soup is often cold or too salty. What will you have to begin with, and what do you say if the soup arrives like that? What do you think of this place?

player: Per cominciare prendo il pane e il prosciutto. Il posto è molto... strano? Ma bello. Ci sono molte sedie!

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work. Your Italian sentences are clear, and you gave your opinion of the place with \"strano ma bello\". Next time, try the words Bettina used for the courses.

objectiveResults.feedback: Your Italian is good and you said what you will have, but the phrase wanted here is "come antipasto", as in "Come antipasto prendo il pane e il prosciutto."
Bettina wants to know what you would say if the soup arrived cold or too salty, so tell her what is wrong with it. She will ask again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Bettina what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Bettina asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Bettina that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: You sit at a tavolo by the finestra, under the stelle. Bettina writes your nome in a libro where every riga already says prenotato, in a hand nobody has met. The cucina is three sandwiches away, which she counts as a long walk.
npc.native: Il pane e il prosciutto, bene, e sì, qui ci sono molte sedie! Io prendo il pane come antipasto, e mio cugino prende la zuppa come primo. Ma la zuppa di mio cugino è sempre fredda, e la mia è troppo salata. Che cosa prende lei, che cosa dice se la sua zuppa è così, e come le sembra il mio lavoro?
npc.translation: The bread and the ham, good, and yes, there are many chairs here! I have the bread as a starter, and my cousin has the soup as a first course. But my cousin's soup is always cold, and mine is too salty. What will you have, what do you say if your soup is like that, and what do you think of my job?

player: Come antipasto vorrei il pane. Ma scusi, il pane è freddo e il prosciutto è troppo salato!

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You ordered your starter politely and complained about the food clearly, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said what you would have to start with, using "Come antipasto vorrei il pane".
Well done: you told Bettina the bread is cold and the ham is too salty.

npc.narrative: Bettina carries the piatto away con calma, like a bishop crossing a tavolo. Outside the finestra the stelle are out, and she counts three people passing, which pleases her. Every sedia in the room holds a reservation, ancora unclaimed.
npc.native: Benissimo, come antipasto lei vuole il pane, e ha ragione: il pane è freddo e il prosciutto è troppo salato! Scusi, porto subito un pane caldo. Che cosa fa lei di bello in questa città, e che cosa pensa di un ristorante con molte sedie e nessun cliente?
npc.translation: Very good, as a starter you want the bread, and you are right: the bread is cold and the ham is too salty! Sorry, I'll bring a warm bread right away. What do you do that is nice in this town, and what do you think of a restaurant with many chairs and no customers?

player: Grazie! Io non abito qui, sono in viaggio. Faccio una passeggiata lunga. Penso che il ristorante è un po' triste senza clienti.

npc.narrative: You sit at the tavolo nearest the porta, where a candela burns beside a reserved card older than the soffitto. Bettina counts you, then the sedie, and looks piano disappointed by the total. Outside, on this sera, the stelle are out and the strada is empty.
npc.native: Lei è in viaggio, che bello! Una passeggiata lunga sono almeno dieci panini, e io non esco mai dal ristorante. Ha ragione, il posto è un po' triste, ma tutti i tavoli sono prenotati. Dove va lei, che cosa vede sulla strada, e che cosa mangia quando cammina? Può chiedere qualcosa anche a me sul mio lavoro.
npc.translation: You are travelling, how lovely! A long walk is at least ten sandwiches, and I never leave the restaurant. You are right, the place is a bit sad, but all the tables are booked. Where are you going, what do you see on the road, and what do you eat when you walk? You can ask me something about my work too.

player: Vado a casa, ma è molto lontano. Sulla strada vedo alberi e mucche. Lei perché non esce mai?

npc.narrative: The stelle hang over the finestra while Bettina counts something on her dita, with great calma. Fuori, one persona passes, poi nessuno. She straightens a tovagliolo at a tavolo that has been booked since the first giorno.
npc.native: Alberi e mucche, che bello! Casa sua è lontana, sono almeno quaranta panini. Io non esco mai perché un cliente può arrivare, e io non sono qui. Stasera passano sette persone, e sette è un numero dispari, per fortuna! Com'è la sua casa, e chi aspetta lei là? Che cosa vuole sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Trees and cows, how lovely! Your home is far, it is at least forty sandwiches. I never go out because a customer might arrive, and I would not be here. Tonight seven people pass, and seven is an odd number, luckily! What is your home like, and who is waiting for you there? What do you want to know about my work?

player: La mia casa è piccola, con un giardino. Mi aspetta il mio gatto! Lei ha un animale?

npc.narrative: The notte is clear, and the stelle hang over the ristorante like clienti who have not sat down. Bettina leans on a sedia and counts you due volte, just to be sure. Behind the bancone, a piccolo vaso of water catches the luce.
npc.native: Un giardino piccolo e un gatto, che bella casa! Sì, io ho un animale: un pesce rosso, e ha un tavolo prenotato dal primo giorno. Come si chiama il suo gatto, e che cosa fa in giardino la sera? Che cosa vuole sapere del mio lavoro e del mio pesce?
npc.translation: A small garden and a cat, what a lovely home! Yes, I have an animal: a goldfish, and he has had a table booked since the first day. What is your cat called, and what does he do in the garden in the evening? What do you want to know about my work and my fish?
